Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said at his Friday press conference ⁠that Joao Pedro, Maxence Lacroix and Reece ⁠James remain ⁠sidelined ​for Saturday’s Premier League clash with Leeds ⁠at Stamford Bridge, while Jorrel Hato and ⁠Jamie Gittens are also ​unavailable. However, Emiliano Martínez is available after his head injury and Moises Caicedo’s minutes were managed while on international duty with Ecuador so he should be fit to play.

Overlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted.

Just ask right-back Ben White, who – with Riccardo Calafiori on the left – has been an important figure in Arsenal’s superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: “Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager. To play full-back for him, you’ve got to be a centre-midfielder, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10.”

Between them, White and Calafiori have contributed to six goals for Arsenal already in the Premier League this season (White: three assists; Calafiori: one goal, two assists). No other defender has registered more than three goal involvements so far. The Arsenal duo are a great illustration of the impact full-backs can have. But, with the position more demanding than ever before, how does each Premier League team deploy theirs?

Read the latest insight from the Opta Analyst:

Nunes and Khusanov doubtful for visit of Fulham

Enzo Maresca confirmed Matheus Nunes and Abdukodir Khusanov are both doubts for Manchester City’s clash with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. The City coach cut a relaxed figure when asked about the three successive league defeats his team suffered before the international break, believing his team are progressing nicely.

He said: “I was not thinking we were doing everything well when we won games, and I’m also not thinking we’re doing everything wrong when we’re losing games.

“We’ve played 16 official games and we’ve won 12, so 70 per cent. If you tell me this is [will happen] in the next 16 games, I will sign! My view is probably different from everyone else’s view. For me it’s just the beginning of something long. I’m very happy in the way we’re working while also being concerned about the things we need to do better.

“It’s a matter of balance that we need to improve. We review things. The idea is to continue in attack in the same way, creating chances, but finding a balance when we defend.”

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola fears Mauricio Pochettino will have a tactical advantage over him on Sunday because the new Manchester United manager is coming in fresh.

Pochettino will be taking charge of United for the first time since leaving his role as USA national team coach to replace the sacked Michael Carrick.

With little to go on as to how Pochettino will setup his United side, Iraola is guessing.

“We’ve faced each other. Obviously he has a lot of Premier League games that we can look at, and we can look at games in the US, but they still have this small advantage,” said Iraola. “We don’t have references to prepare because they can go different ways that we don’t actually know.

“The staff have been working with them, so they are going to arrive well prepared. We don’t have the references that we have against other teams.”

One advantage Iraola could have looked to exploit was the drone footage posted on YouTube of Pochettino’s first training session at Carrington, but the Liverpool manager was quick to criticise the YouTube channel that posted the video.

“They were sending me the footage yesterday, but I think the important thing about this is that it shouldn’t be legal. It happened to Manchester United but it could happen to me in a training session in the future,” he said.

“It isn’t about the advantage, it is the fact that there is a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect.”

Manchester United do not intend to take legal action ⁠against a drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session, but warned that anyone responsible for further incidents would face ⁠significant legal and financial ⁠risk.

The operator, ​who identifies himself as Colin but has not disclosed his full name, apologised earlier today for what he called a “total error ⁠of judgement” and removed the footage from his YouTube channel.

A club source told Reuters there ‌was no security breach at the Carrington site and that, while it was unclear whether the incident breached drone laws, United believed it had ​breached a number of other laws.

The club source said the operator had done the right thing by apologising and removing the content without being contacted by United. Reuters

Pochettino finishes on a question about whether or not the timing is right for him to manage United by saying: “A club like Manchester United, you cannot turn down.”

Asked whether or not he missed the day-to-day club of club management, Pochettino replies: “Of course. We were missing [the pressure] a lot. We are animals of the grass. We like to feel the grass, we like to smell the grass and try to help the players improve everyday. It’s true that it’s a different job when you’re in the national teams, but at the same time you learn a lot and we are much better coaches now.”

Asked whether he thought was fit enough, Pochettino says: “When we arrive, I think we found a group of players that we propose to do the football that we feel. To be brave and be Manchester United. It is about proposing that idea to be brave and take it to the field.”

He adds that data, such as the running stats referenced in the question, needs to be taken in context and while it can tell a story it is not the whole story.

Hinting at the question that plagued Ruben Amorim about whether he is coach or manager: “I was in all my career a coach, head coach, manager. It does not change too much.”

However, Pochettino also makes it clear he expects to be a part of the recruitment process: “I know in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that affect the squad.”

Pochettino confirms Bruno Fernandes will remain as captain: “Bruno is our captain and a very important player but other players have to feel they are important from the bottom to the top.

“We spoke yesterday, I spent three hours chatting with all the players individually yesterday. I think I missed some injured players but in the next few days we will talk with everyone.

“It was very nice contact. It is important to listen to the players and what they need to say about areas on and off the field.”

“I don’t think too much about the past,” adds Pochettino. “It is about building our own way here. Of course, we feel the support from the club and we start to work.

“The past is not going to help, to think about yesterday. We have been speaking to the players and the most important thing is to think about the next action.

“We feel the support and we are going to work really hard to help the players to perform. That is the priority.”

Pochettino says his target, after getting over the jet lag, is to get too know the people around the club and his players. He adds that his target is to “try and from the beginning have an impact. It is important to have a positive impact, that is our most important job.”

Pochettino is happy to be here, which is a good start. Asked how you create a culture, he says: “The players need to buy into the idea that we need to improve, that is our job. The job is to find a way from Sunday to perform and to start to get the results that that [United] historically need because Manchester United need to be in a different place than they are now.”

Mauricio Pochettino has just walked into the press room…

David Moyes has confirmed Jack Grealish is “fit and available” for Everton’s trip to Brentford on Monday, having missed the past four games through a combination of illness and for disciplinary reasons. Grealish played in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Derby last week and issued an apology for not being able to help the team. “He’s back in training and back in around the team,” said Moyes, who received a presentation from captain James Tarkowski and former player Leon Osman before his press conference on Friday. Moyes will manage Everton for the 593th time on Monday - breaking Harry Catterick’s club record.

Email from Dean Kinsella: “Well that Nation’s Cup draw couldn’t really have panned out much better for England. Norway (except for the big guy upfront) shouldn’t be too great an obstacle. While the two other main contenders, France and Spain battle it out. I’ll get the silver polish out.”

It’s like Dean has no experience of watching England at all. More broadly, as much as the Nations League is a significant improvement on international friendlies, do we count it as silverware? Would winning it be a bigger achievement than Le Tournoi?

Now news from Poland, where the national football federation says it has suspended 10 players competing in the lower divisions for suspected match-fixing.

The Polish Football Association (PZPN) said in a statement that the players were playing in the third division and lower, but did not indicate how long they will be suspended. Associated Press

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois has signed a contract ⁠extension until June 2028, the La Liga club have announced.

Courtois’ ​previous contract had been ​due to expire in June 2027.

Lisa Baum is 19, for the next few days at least, but you wouldn’t know it. The Germany forward plays with a maturity that explains why she was handed her Arsenal debut in their opening game of the season, less than two months after joining.

Baum had been told that the 2025 European champions had a vision for her but that coming in as a young player she would have to be patient. Ten minutes into her debut against Brighton, in Crawley, the young winger scored what would be the winning goal.

“It was unbelievable,” says Baum, speaking in a small meeting room at Arsenal’s London Colney training ground with a maturity that matches her play. “Everything just went so quick. I just shot, my brain was just switched off, it just came out.”

Read Suzanne Wrack’s full interview with Lisa Baum:

I’m being substituted out of blog action for a while, leaving you in the capable hands of Tom Bassam for the next next couple of hours. Bye for now!

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton coach, has given his press conference ahead of the game against Hull, and explained how, when and why he punishes players for not being sufficiently committed to their counter-pressing:

double quotation markCounter-pressing is a law for us. Counter-pressing is not a decision you can do. It’s something you can do when you have a good day, when you have a bad day, when you’re in a bad mood, when you’re ready for a game or training, you can do it every day. It’s a non-negotiable for us. If you have the feeling the players are not on it then yeah, in some moments the players have to run. But we use it more in pre-season. As long as I’m happy with the counter-pressing we don’t need it.

Hürzeler says he’s not worried about drones taking footage of his training sessions. “No, because we have an airport next to us. So if they put a drone up I’m sure the drone won’t exist long, because it can cause some bad consequences. We don’t have this problem. We have other problems, with the aeroplanes, sometimes with the wind.

With the Brighton owner, Tony Bloom, having suggested this week that he could one day move to Bayern Munich, Hürzeler has committed his immediate future to the club, saying he “still has the feeling that I’m not done”:

double quotation markTo me it’s a privilege to work here. And of course in my time here there were a lot of rumours but I’m always fully committed to this club. I never had this feeling of leaving, because the club gives me a lot. I still go to bed and have the feeling that I’m not done. I still think there’s potential to get out of this team, to get out of this club.

As one of the most meticulous coaches in soccer, Mikel Arteta likes to have every base covered in his quest to win titles with Arsenal. Turns out his players giving away squad secrets through an online fantasy game is an area he hasn’t been able to control, reports Associated Press.

In the latest example of a growing issue for Premier League managers, Arsenal winger Christos Tzolis unwittingly gave away a clue that he would be returning to action after a month-long injury absence by selecting himself in his own team in the Fantasy Premier League game played by more than 11 million people worldwide.

That information was picked up by some of the fantasy game’s eagle-eyed content creators and, sure enough, Tzolis was named in Arsenal’s team the very next day for the English champions’ 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield.

Guarding team selections is a big deal in soccer – hence limits to the presence of media at practice sessions and the furore that erupted when Southampton was found to have used an analyst to carry out the unauthorized filming of opponents in training last season. So Arteta has taken measures to combat the problem, with The Athletic reporting that he has banned Arsenal’s players from including themselves or their teammates in their fantasy lineups.

On Friday, Arteta spoke about the issue, saying it has had an impact “with Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well.”

“Constantly they are asking me about the lineups as well because they want to know,” he said with a laugh, before adopting a more serious tone. “It is a topic, a thing that is happening in our society right now and it’s something new — we’ve haven’t [previously] dealt with it. We need to put new things in place.”

Arteta insisted that “confidentiality is something critical” for teams wanting to be successful. “Because it’s about trust, about what you are trying to do, and that should be kept as a huge secret,” he said. “And we’ll take measures to make sure it doesn’t happen again.”

Earlier this month, the BBC reported that an email was sent by Chelsea to its staff, warning them about the possible consequences of making team selections in Fantasy Premier League using their inside information about injuries.

That came after Chelsea striker Joao Pedro was removed from the fantasy teams of teammate Morgan Rogers and other staff members before news of an injury to the Brazilian had been made public. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso later said he was “not into the fantasy team thing,” so was unaware.

Tonda Eckert has signed a new contract at Southampton, extending his stay until 2029. Eckert, the architect of the so-called Spygate case, which saw Saints kicked out of last season’s Championship play-offs and begin this season with a four-point deduction, said he is grateful for the continued support of owner Dragan Solak, group technical director Johannes Spors and chief executive Phil Parsons.

“There is a lot that has happened in the last 12 months, but the commitment from the club, from Dragan, Johannes and Phil, and the supporters, means everything to me. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through – there is a lot more to come.”

Southampton, who are seventh in the Championship, five points off the summit, host Derby this Saturday.

The 33-year-old’s previous contract was due to expire at the end of the season. Despite the well-documented lows of last season, has picked up 96 points since initially taking charge on an interim basis 12 months ago, at least 12 more than any other club across the period.

Fulham’s Álvaro Arbeloa has given his Friday press conference ahead of his team’s visit to Manchester City, against whom they have lost their last 20 games, and he has heaped praise on someone who is likely to be very busy: Calvin Bassey, who has been linked with a move to Manchester United.

double quotation markI’m going to be really clear: he is very, very important. He’s one of our captains, and from the first day that I arrived and I saw how good he is, I think he is one of the best centre-backs in the world. So it’s normal that there are so many teams that want Calvin – that, for me, is normal.

I think Calvin is really happy here. He’s so important for us, he’s one of our leaders. I think he’s performing really well. The way that we are playing, I think he can shine because he’s a defender that can defend in a high line. He’s very aggressive, he’s very good with the ball. For me, he’s brilliant as a player, so I am really happy with him, and I hope he will be with us for many years.

Fulham is not a jail – everyone that is here is because they want to be here, because they are happy, because they feel important, because they feel loved. And, for me, this is the most important thing.

MLS business, then, and Jeff Rueter has been musing about Columbus Crew ahead of their play-off fixture against Inter Miami tomorrow:

The Columbus Crew have a more holistic operation than most in MLS. The club as a whole still exists thanks to the dogged efforts of their fervent fanbase that helped block relocation. Their under-19s won the national cup in June, while the developmental Crew 2 made a fourth semi-final berth in five seasons in MLS Next Pro. The first team regularly punches above its weight in MLS, winning the third-most major titles (nine) among MLS originals.

And yet, this year tested the conventions set by team and league alike.

In January, chief soccer officer Issa Tall welcomed the club’s eighth head coach, Henrik Rydström. Having only previously coached in his native Sweden, the 50-year-old used his introductory presser to laud the values of relationism, to praise his predecessor, and to plot a bold course for a new Crew. It was assumed he’d be around a while – the Crew have historically been patient with coaches, needing only seven bosses to navigate their first 30 seasons.

By mid-May, after just 16 games in charge, Rydström was on his way back to Sweden. His five wins were the lowest of the eight full-time Crew coaches. And yet, Saturday sees the Crew begin the MLS Cup Playoffs in a best-of-three matchup with Lionel Messi and Inter Miami.

Here’s the Associated Press take on that Uefa draw:

Spain will face France in the Nations League quarter-finals in a rematch of their World Cup semi-final. England will play Norway in another World Cup rematch, but another matchup between Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé was the standout prospect from the Nations League draw made Friday.

Spain beat France 2-0 in July on its way to a World Cup title. England beat Norway 2-1 in the quarter-finals. The other quarterfinal pairings Friday were the Netherlands against title holder Portugal and Belgium against Germany.

The winners advance to the Final Four mini tournament from 9-13 June to be hosted by one of the teams. The host should be decided on 7 December at Uefa’s executive committee meeting in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

These quarter-finals have been set a high bar by the previous edition in March 2025. Then, three of the four quarterfinals went to extra time in the second leg — two to penalty shootouts — and included 3-3 draws between Spain and the Netherlands and Germany against Italy, when the Italians trailed 3-0 at halftime. Portugal advanced to the Final Four by beating Denmark 5-2 after extra time in the second leg.

Belarus was drawn to play Israel in the promotion-relegation playoffs for a place in second tier League B. Neither team has played games on home soil for at least the last three years for security and political reasons. Current Uefa rules mean each must choose a neutral venue for their “home” leg, which opens the possibility of playing both games in the same stadium back-to-back.

Back to matters domestic, then, and Kilmarnock manager Neil McCann has spoken about the “insane” pressure heaped on coaches and players in the Scottish Premiership as he prepares to face Aberdeen in the wake of Stephen Robinson’s dismissal, writes the Press Association.

Robinson arrived on the back of sustained success with Motherwell and St Mirren but barely got out of November in his first full season at Pittodrie. Killie sit bottom of the Premiership, two points behind the Dons, who travel to Rugby Park with former Vaduz and Luzern head coach Mario Frick at the helm.

“The pressures are insane at times,” McCann said. “I just feel it was a tough situation for Stevie. He’s a really good coach and I was really sad to see him lose his job. I suppose that’s where we are in football. There seems to be a real appetite for applying pressure these days.

“You’ve got to be brave to be a professional athlete these days. There’s a lot of scrutiny now. How people consume their media is very different to when I played. Everybody’s got an opinion and it’s quite vocal as well because it’s accessible more than ever now, even to the players.

“I ask the players not to get involved in it but it’s not like my time, there is an acceptance that there will be more to take in there. Maybe that’s where the extra pressure’s coming from. The external noise can’t affect the game. If you let it affect you, then that’s down to you.”

And that concludes today’s draw, which was supposed to take half an hour and did indeed take precisely 30 minutes. A triumph of draw-planning.

Netherlands or Portugal v Spain or France Belgium or Germany v Norway or England

Still one more draw to draw, to decide who the winning quarter-finalists will face in the semi-finals.

The Nations League quarter-finals will look like this, with England handed a replay of their 2026 World Cup quarter-final against Norway, and Spain playing France!

Spain v France Norway v England Netherlands v Portugal Belgium v Germany

Once again, first legs on 25 or 27 March. Second legs on 28 or 30 March.

And now we reach the serious business: the eight teams still in contention to lift the trophy next June, at [major venue tbc]! Who will it be?

The second and final Nations League play-off draw has happened, and this is what it’s thrown up:

Bosnia-Herzegovina v Denmark Hungary v Serbia Republic of Ireland v Croatia Slovenia v Wales

Again, first legs on 25 or 27 March. Second legs on 28 or 30 March.

Next up, the League A/B play-offs. Again, they’ll draw the four unseeded teams first, as they will play the first leg at home, followed by the four seeded teams.

The League B/C play-off pairings have been decided, and here they are:

Cyprus v North Macedonia Estonia v Romania Faroe Islands v Georgia Belarus v Israel

First legs on 25 or 27 March. Second legs on 28 or 30 March.

OK, they’re ready to go in Nyon. The League B/C play-off draw is about to happen!

Nations League dates for your diary: the first-leg matches of the quarter-finals and all play-offs are “in principle” scheduled for either Thursday 25 March or Saturday 27 March 2027. The return legs will take place on Sunday 28 March and Tuesday 30 March.

The semi-finals will be played on Wednesday 9 June at 9pm CET and Thursday 10 June, also at 9pm CET. The final will be played on Sunday 13 again at 9pm CET with the third-place match preceding it, at 3pm that afternoon. If those matches end in a draw there will be 30 minutes of extra time, followed if necessary by penalties – except in the third-place play-off, which will go straight to penalties without the extra time.

You’ll be wanting to know the Nations League draw order of business, and I can help. They’ll start with the League B/C play-offs, for which the seeded teams are Israel, Romania, Georgia and North Macedonia, and the unseeded teams are Estonia, Belarus, Faroe Islands and Cyprus. In this and all draws, teams who were in the same group cannot be paired again.

Then the A/B play-offs. The seeded teams are Denmark, Croatia, Wales and Serbia, and the unseeded teams Slovenia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Hungary and the Republic of Ireland.

Then the quarter-finals. The seeds are England, Portugal, France and Germany. Unseeded sides are Spain, Belgium, Netherlands and Norway.

Coming up at 11am GMT: the Uefa Nations League knockout stage and play-off draw! Uefa say this will take about half an hour and will include the draw for the quarter- and semi-finals. Wales and the Republic of Ireland are among the teams in the League A/B play-off draw, with the Welsh among the seeded teams, while England are among the seeds for the quarter-final.

Here’s Ed Aarons with more on Arsenal’s fitness issues:

Mikel Arteta has admitted Bukayo Saka may not return before Christmas as the Arsenal forward continues his rehabilitation from a thigh injury.

Saka has been out since limping off against Bayern Munich at the end of last month, and it is understood he has yet to resume light training. Arteta revealed more tests during the international break confirmed the England forward did not need surgery and that he is expected to be out for another four weeks.

When asked whether Saka could be fit for the game against Manchester United on 20 December, Arteta was unsure. “I cannot be that specific,” he said. “In four weeks’ time a lot of things can happen. Maybe it is three and then it is five.”

Mikel Arteta has given an update on the fitness of his players ahead of Saturday’s trip to Newcastle, with the centre back William Saliba available after recovering from a back injury ⁠sustained during the World Cup but Martin Zubimendi out with a hamstring injury.

Saliba was forced off the field ⁠during France’s World Cup ⁠semi-final loss to ​Spain in July, and underwent a long rehabilitation programme. The 25-year-old appeared for Arsenal’s Under-21 side earlier this month, and recently played a friendly ⁠against Watford behind closed doors.

“He’s ready. He’s in a good condition. He played two games, one behind closed doors and one more official and he did really ⁠well,” Arteta told a press conference.

Arsenal have excelled in Saliba’s absence, with close-season signing Ezri Konsa slotting in ​alongside Gabriel at the heart of the defence.

The ‌Frenchman was a standout performer ‌in their run to the Premier League title last season, but is not guaranteed to immediately reclaim ‌his place in an Arsenal defence that has conceded only five goals in 10 league games this season.

Arsenal, however, will be without defensive midfielder Zubimendi for a few weeks after the Spain international suffered a hamstring injury during Sunday’s Nations League clash with England.

Winger Bukayo Saka, who is out with a quadriceps injury, is still four weeks away from a possible return, the ​manager confirmed

A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the Manchester City forward withdrew his support for the prosecution, reports the Press Association.

Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool Magistrates’ Court on Friday in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting abuse during the Premier League match between Liverpool and Semenyo’s former club Bournemouth at Anfield on August 15 last year.

But Simon Jones, prosecuting, said: “Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him. In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case.”

District Judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour.

Semenyo, who left Bournemouth for Manchester City in January, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mr Mogan was taken to hospital after suffering a seizure.

The court had heard Mr Mogan, in a wheelchair, shouted at Semenyo as he went to take a throw-in about 30 minutes into the game. Witnesses also said they saw him throw his chewing gum at the footballer. Semenyo reported the incident to the match referee and Mr Mogan was removed from the stadium at half-time.

Mr Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, told police in an interview that Semenyo had called him a cripple after he shouted at the player to “hurry up”. Mr Mogan declined to comment as he left court.

For the Liverpool fan who has everything, a commemorative Istanbul 2005 boxed set including a replica 2005 jersey hand-signed by the starting 11, three substitutes and manager Rafa Benítez, plus five A4 art prints, a mini replica UCL magnet and a commemorative 20th Anniversary coin. Down from £1,500 (one thousand and five hundred pounds!) to just £1,050. Also available in their 30% off everything Black Friday sale, an LFC YNWA Padel racket, down to just £49 (plis p&p)! “Built for all-round performance, it offers a stable and user-friendly feel for club and recreational sports … Use bag to protect racker [sic] when not in use.”

While we wait for press conferences to start and some kind of news to happen, I’ll be perusing some clubs’ Black Friday sales for discounted items of questionable merit. Like, for example, a limited edition print of a drawing of Aaron Ramsdale, hand signed by the actual Aaron Ramsdale. “Elegantly mounted and framed, this unique print will infuse your space with sophisticated Arsenal charm,” the Premier League champions proclaim. Only 100 available! And down from £300 to just £150! Also at Arsenal, a “pet bib”, down from £12 to £8.40, which “features a heat-applied cannon at front and an elastic neckband for dog and cat-approved everyday comfort (and cuteness)”. A bib? For a pet?

Now I’ve warmed you up, Simon Burnton is here to take over and get into the good stuff.

I only got eight this week, can you do any better? It’s sports quiz of the week:

A drone operator who filmed Manchester United’s training ⁠session this week has apologised for what he called a “total error of judgment” and removed ⁠the footage from ⁠his ​YouTube channel.

The footage, filmed at United’s Carrington training ground during new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first training ⁠session on Thursday, was uploaded online under the username CC Overview. In a statement posted on his YouTube channel ⁠on Friday, the drone operator said that while the flight ​was legal under drone regulations, ‌filming the session ‌had been “unethical”.

“My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his ‌United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time,” he said. “I fully accept it was unethical on my part. I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely ‌hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”

The operator added that he had wrongly ​assumed only warm-up activities would be visible and that the training session would be open to various media outlets. He also said neither Liverpool nor any other football club had been involved ⁠in his decision to film at Carrington. “The video has been ​removed from ​my channel,” he said.

Bruno Guimarães to feel the heat on Tyneside, Alex Scott’s return further cheers Cherries and Manchester City face favourite whipping boys… here are your 10 things to look out for in the Premier League this weekend:

Fifa news … Kozo Tashima said he hasn’t talked yet with fellow Fifa presidential race challenfer Philippe Diallo, but he’s willing to work with the Frenchman to defeat Gianni Infantino’s bid for a controversial fourth term.

Tashima and Diallo are two long-shot candidates to replace Infantino in an election set for 18 March. So there’s still plenty time to sway Fifa’s 211 member federations.

“We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he’s a great person to team up with,” Tashima said in comments translated from Japanese. “I’m not looking at Diallo as opposition. I just want to change Fifa. Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management. I do trust him. At this point I’m not think about withdrawing.”

Tashima, who repeated the words “integrity, fairness, trust and transparency” when asked why he decided to stand, is going against the endorsement of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), which last month pledged support for Infantino — with Infantino on hand at the meeting in Tokyo.

“I just don’t only want to be the Fifa president, my intention was to make Fifa better,” Tashima added. “Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organisation.

“I believe the worst outcome would be for him (Infantino) to remain in office without an election,” he said. “I believe this is a test of whether Fifa truly has the capacity for self-reform. “He’s done a lot of things to make us doubt his integrity,” Tashima said, adding that income from the World Cup – or anywhere else – “is not an Infantino asset. It belongs to Fifa.”

In a three-candidate election, votes from two-thirds of the eligible members are needed to win in the first round. For the second round, the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated and a simple majority will win. In a two-candidate race, Infantino would need votes from 106 of the 211 member federations to win re-election.

Footage from Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session as Manchester United manager has appeared online after being captured by a drone operator. A 12-minute video of the session was posted on to YouTube by an account called CC OVERVIEW after being captured at United’s Carrington training ground. Pochettino and his United players can be seen in the video, with the squad having been divided into three groups.

On the post, the drone operator wrote: “For the people asking about legality. It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it. The drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn’t fly over anyone or even near anyone so was a perfectly legal flight going by the CAA rules that regulates drone usage.

“The drone is correctly labelled, and I hold all the relevant licences, public liability and insurance required. As for leaking team news/tactics, it was half an hour into the manager’s first training session, there are many media there so certainly won’t be the only footage of training released.”

Manchester United have declined to comment.

Pochettino was taking his first training session after being appointed as United’s new head coach last week, succeeding Michael Carrick who was sacked with the club in the relegation zone during this international window. Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, having taken charge of the United States for the final time in their 2-0 win over Haiti, which finished in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time. His first match in charge will be a visit to old rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon. Press Association

Thanks international football, the FA Cup and the Manchester United brains trust, that was fun. We’ll see you again soon. Now it’s time to lock in on pure club action for the foreseeable.

There are seven Premier League fixtures on Saturday, including five in the traditional 3pm slot, two more on Sunday and then Monday night football too. The Championship is also back with 11 fixtures on Saturday and a midday Lancashire derby on Sunday, completing a full slate of EFL after League One and League Two gamely held the fort for the past two weeks – manna from heaven.

Two top-flight clubs come into this post-Nations League bloc with a new man in the dugout. The aforementioned United and fellow basement dwellers Crystal Palace. Thomas Frank’s Eagles go to Coventry (a team managed by Frank Lampard), which looks like both a tricky test and a presentable opportunity for the new man in charge at Palace. Mauricio Pochettino gets a nice easy one first up, away at Liverpool.

Pochettino has already had a taste of the scrutiny that being in charge at Old Trafford brings, with part of his first training session captured by a drone enthusiast and shared on YouTube. Safe to say, people weren’t going to those lengths to see how Tim Ream’s ball progression drills went in USMNT camp.

If we get anymore high-profile drone action or other newsworthy football items this blog will be across it, plus we’ll have updates from the various press conferences taking place today. Do follow along and you can get in touch via the email link at the top of the page.

#779. Percy Jackson’s Walker Scobell Reacts to His Dad’s Looks Going Viral

Percy Jackson and the Olympians’ Walker Scobell shared his candid reaction to his dad’s looks going viral in an exclusive interview with E! News.

Some pop culture moments just catch like lightning.

And for Percy Jackson’s Walker Scobell, the innocent decision to bring his (we’ll say it) noticeably handsome dad Pete Scobell along on a Good Morning America appearance Nov. 9 led to whirlwind virality, with “hot dad” memes quickly abounding.

For Walker, however, it’s an internet storm he knows he just needs to weather.

“Oh my god, don’t say it, he’s over there somewhere,” Walker lamented during his exclusive interview with E! News, noting his dad was present in the room. “I'm aware of it. He's aware of it, too. He thought it was hilarious.”

And though Pete didn’t intentionally try to steal his son’s thunder—nor his Master Bolt—Walker joked his dad’s newfound fame is getting to his head.

“He walks, his shoulders are back and he's standing up a little taller,” the 17-year-old quipped, before clarifying, “No, he just thinks it's really funny. I think he's handling it well. He kind of makes a bunch of jokes about it. My mom and my brother and sister were making jokes about it.”

But as it turns out, he isn’t the only young star who found that the public became enamored with the block from whence the chip came.

“I’d actually talked to McKenna Grace about this because her dad has also had a similar treatment online,” Walker revealed. “So, when I saw her for the first time in a couple of years the other day, that was kind of the first thing we said to each other was like, ‘Yeah, our dads.’”

For his costar Tamara Smart—who plays Zeus’ daughter Thalia Grace in the series—the online perception of Pete couldn’t have fallen farther from the actual tree.

“I think it's ironic, too, because he is the most chill, humble guy,” she said. “You just see him hanging around set and he's so sweet. So, to go viral on the morning show is just incredible.”

As for Walker, he’s taking it all in stride. After all, he doesn’t need an oracle to tell him his dad’s looks only bode well for his own future.

“It’s a compliment,” The Adam Project alum affirmed. “Hopefully I’ll look like him.”

But while the actor may have had trouble wrapping his head around his dad’s new claim to fame, he had much more luck getting in touch with his character, Percy Jackson, as he prepared for the third installment of the Disney+ show. After all, he a lot of source material to work with in the form of Rick Riordan’s books.

“I'm lucky because I'm the only character in the show that for these first five books, I know everything that my character is thinking all the time,” Walker explained. “I can always go back to the book and be like, ‘What was he thinking, and what does he think in situations like this?’ So, I feel like I just say what I think he would be thinking out loud or try to show it on my face.”

So, don’t miss Percy Jackson and the Olympians when it hits Disney+ on Nov. 20. And for more electrifying TV to tune into before the end of the year, read on.

Nocturne tells the story of Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber), an ex-soldier turned homicide detective who, tired of working the tough streets of Philadelphia, moves to a small town in Western Pennsylvania for a quiet life. But, as the town and his family come under attack from the diabolically cunning serial killer Jurek Walter (Stephen Graham), Jonah must protect all that he holds dear. When the desperate search for Jurek’s last missing victim forces Jonah to send his surrogate daughter FBI Agent Saga Bauer (Zazie Beetz) up against Jurek, how far will Jonah go?

Bertha Russell changed Society at a cost. Now, her family must reckon with the consequences as Agnes van Rhijn seizes an opportunity to regain her position. Meanwhile, Marian forges a new path for herself, and Peggy works to be accepted by her future in-laws. In this new era, you must be careful what you wish for.

St. Denis Medical is a mockumentary about an underfunded, understaffed Oregon hospital where the dedicated doctors and nurses try their best to treat patients while maintaining their own sanity. In season three, romantic entanglements and personal struggles complicate relationships in the Emergency Department, pushing some St. Denis employees to the brink.

The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins (NBC) - Nov. 2

Season two of the hit comedy returns with the unlikely duo of former football star Reggie Dinkins (Tracy Morgan) and documentarian Arthur Tobin (Daniel Radcliffe), both still chasing redemption and still making a mess of it. With the help of his family, Reggie will continue his quest to recapture his past glory.

In season two, Santi takes the next step in his pursuit of professional golf, only to discover how quickly the game changes when talent becomes expectation. As Santi chases his dream, Pryce Cahill (Owen Wilson) finds himself wondering what might still be possible for him. Urged on by his former rival Clark Ross (Timothy Olyphant), Pryce does something nobody expects: he bets on himself, launching an improbable comeback in hopes of becoming the oldest golfer ever to win a major. But the road back proves far harder than he imagined. And the closer Pryce gets to the golfer he once was, the more he is forced to confront why he never fulfilled the promise everyone once saw in him. With brilliant new coach Amanda (Rhea Seehorn) and trusted caddie Mitts (Marc Maron) in his corner, Pryce sets out to prove — to the golf world and, more importantly, to himself — that maybe he really was as good as everyone always said he was.

The lawyers of Grant, Ronson & Greene are back for another season of scandals, secrets, and stilettos. As new allegiances form, friendships are tested and a shocking revelation threatens the very existence of the firm.

The Remarried Princess (Hulu & Disney+) - Nov. 4

Based on the hit Naver Webtoon of the same name, The Remarried Empress follows the strained relationship of beloved Empress Navier and her husband Emperor Sovieshu of the Eastern Kingdom. With anxieties rising across the kingdom, the couple’s relationship begins to fracture when Sovieshu falls in love with a runaway slave and attempts to move heaven and earth to win her heart. Unwilling to compromise her dignity, Navier acquiesces to the emperor’s requests on one condition – that she be allowed to remarry rival Crown Prince Heinrey of the Western Kingdom. What follows is a tale of love, lust and regret that threatens the fate of an entire kingdom as Navier strives to reclaim her power.

The documentary traces Muhammad Ali’s coming of age story, following a young Cassius Clay through the personal, professional and political battles he fought inside and outside the ring. Set against a changing America, The Greatest follows a once-in-a-generation talent fighting for the right to become his own man. Through the fights that made him a champion and the convictions that made him an icon, a young man from Louisville transforms himself into Muhammad Ali, the greatest of all time.

Taken: Natalee Holloway (Netflix) - Nov. 4

On May 30, 2005, 18-year-old Natalee Holloway vanished on a high school graduation trip to Aruba—and never came home. What followed was years of unanswered questions, a missing teenager, and a mother's relentless fight for the truth. Now, over 20 years later, Natalee's mother, Beth, is ready to tell the complete story. With exclusive, unprecedented access to Beth and those who were with Natalee when she vanished, this three-part documentary series is the definitive account of a case that gripped a nation and never let go. It's a story of a mother who refused to stop searching, an investigation that spanned continents, and a daughter whose memory endures. This is Natalee's story, told at last in full.

Helen (Keira Knightley) is still betraying her nation’s secrets to the covert organization she serves: the Black Doves. But after the misadventures of last Christmas, and with her husband Wallace (Andrew Buchan), preparing to become Prime Minister, she is walking a more treacherous line than ever.

Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook (Apple TV) - Nov. 6

The eight-episode series follows Nora Lum, aka Awkwafina, on a cross-country culinary road trip as she attempts to revive her family’s beloved Chinese restaurant.

Wolves Up Close With Bertie Gregory (National Geographic) - Nov. 6

Reconnecting with a pack of wolves he has followed for seven years, Bertie Gregory sets out to capture one of the Arctic’s most dangerous and rarely filmed hunts: wolves taking on a bull moose, prey roughly ten times their size. Led by Kona, a striking white breeding male, the pack faces a critical winter as dwindling food supplies, an encroaching rival wolf and an aging leader threaten its survival.

Charmed By a Southern Monster (Peacock) - Nov. 9

Starring Craig Conover as Hunter Caldwell and Nicole Mattox as Maeve Marchant, the series blends soapy romance, workplace rivalry and small-town mystery.

The story follows Maeve, a brilliant corporate fixer sent to convince and seduce Hunter, a rumored murderer, into selling his family’s estate. But when she discovers that the town’s most feared man may actually be its most misunderstood, and the only person who can protect her from her dangerous ex-boyfriend, Maeve becomes entangled in Hunter’s world. As family secrets and a billion-dollar development deal threaten to unravel their growing connection, she must confront her past and decide how much she’s willing to risk for love.

Whitney Way Thore is stepping into a transformative new chapter. Back in her home state of North Carolina, Whitney has found love with Jake, a man she first met years ago before reconnecting after her return to Charlotte. As their relationship deepens, Whitney is rediscovering her confidence through dance, exploring new possibilities on her health journey, and taking meaningful steps toward the future she’s always wanted, including her biggest dream of becoming a mom.

Picking up after the gut-wrenching mid-series finale, Tony Baddingham and Declan O'Hara's battle for the Cotswolds crown reaches fever pitch, while Rupert Campbell-Black is forced to confront his own personal demons. Against a backdrop of hedonistic parties, Bonfire Night chaos, the Hampshire Hunt Ball and a turbulent Christmas, affairs unravel, alliances fracture and rivalries intensify. Caught in the middle of the frenzied franchise war, Taggie O'Hara must find the courage to follow her heart, while those around her face the consequences of ambition, power and secrets that can no longer remain hidden. But as series two draws to a close, who will get their happy ending?

From Ron Howard, the documentary explores the life, career, and cultural impact of legendary American photographer Richard Avedon.

The Good Daughter is a suspenseful thriller wrapped in a deeply emotional story about love, family and resilience. Sisters Charlotte (Meghann Fahy) and Samantha (Rose Byrne) Quinn have spent the last 20 years trying to piece together the lives that were fractured by a single night of violence. When another attack splinters the small town of Pikeville, Charlotte – now a lawyer like her father – is the first witness on the scene. As the case unfolds and twists through painful memories and buried secrets, what emerges is not just a story of survival, but of enduring ties between a father and his daughters, and the complex bond between sisters.

After a reunion where the status of friendships and situationships remained ambiguous, the Charmers are determined to define their relationships and mend wounds. However, when true feelings bubble up and juicy rumors catch fire, the group seeks to unveil the truth – even if it costs them more than just friendships.

Three years into their jobs as response officers, Constables Grace Ellis, Tommy Foster, and Annie Conlon are operating at their limit, facing a new threat on the streets that the police can barely control. Meanwhile the murder trial of Gerry Cliff exposes a dangerous and long-buried secret that leads to chaos both inside the police, and across the criminal underworld. As they grapple with big decisions about their future, Grace, Tommy and Annie must find the courage to face the greatest threat they have ever encountered: the truth.

Each episode of the drama unfolds across three timelines of a heist: the 12 months of planning, the 12 hours of the heist, and the 12 days following the heist. The series follows a disgraced FBI agent (Anthony Mackie) and an American career criminal (Jamie Dornan) who play a zero-sum game of cat and mouse across Europe. At the center of it all is the daring, epic raid on a bank vault deep beneath the streets of Zurich.

Expedition: Saving Our Seas (National Geographic) - Nov. 13

The documentary follows teams of National Geographic Explorers as they investigate our global Ocean, from seashore to seafloor and pole to pole. Combining cutting-edge technology with the knowledge of coastal communities, they chase the discoveries and solutions needed to protect our Oceans at a critical moment.

Homicide for the Holidays (Oxygen) - Nov. 14

The holidays are supposed to be the most wonderful time of the year. But for some families, cherished celebrations become the backdrop for unimaginable violence. Season six of Homicide For The Holidays brings a new batch of deadly deeds to the supposed jolliest time of the year as investigators pursue those responsible and seek justice for families shattered at a time meant for togetherness.

Diane Morgan returns as Philomena Cunk in a new series from Charlie Brooker. Billed as Cunk's most glamorous outing yet, she charts the history of cinema, from the invention of the camera and the New Wave filmmakers of the 1960s right up to the entrance of CGI and what the future of AI holds. Cunk will attempt to demystify it all while sitting in lumpy seats with stale popcorn, asking herself where did cinema come from? And why? What does it want? And why can’t it tell us?

Small Town Trouble: Texas (Bravo) - Nov. 18

Here, perception is everything, temptation is everywhere, and the truth is never as buttoned-up as it looks.

The story of Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison, two hyper-smart, ambitious young idealists who tried to remake the global financial system in the blink of an eye - before they were accused of stealing $8 billion and became Gen Z's own Bonnie & Clyde.

Nelly and Ashanti: We Belong Together (Peacock) - Nov. 19

This season, Ashanti continues to balance motherhood, continuing to perform on stage, and taking control of her musical legacy. Between raising their son, honoring their village, and planning for their future, Nelly and Ashanti discover that belonging together isn’t about standing still; it’s about building a future on their own terms.

#778. Filming training by drones should be illegal - Iraola

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool take on Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United on Sunday

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola says filming with drones around training grounds should be illegal after Mauricio Pochettino's first session as Manchester United boss was captured and uploaded online.

Pochettino and his players were clearly visible in the footage, which was shot above United's Carrington training base from a variety of angles and distances.

The drone operater apologised and later took down the footage, with sources telling BBC Sport they are adamant there was no security breach and that they do not intend to take legal action.

Iraola said he was sent the 12 minutes of footage on Thursday - three days before United travel to Anfield for a Premier League match.

"The important part of this is that it shouldn't be legal," he said on Friday. "It happened to United but it could happen to me.

"Yesterday, when Sky Sports had access to our training and the cameras recorded 15-20 minutes, you know who trained and who didn't.

"It's not the matter of the advantage. It's the fact that someone can do this. There's a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect. I don't think it's nice for any club."

Filming training on a drone 'shouldn't be legal' - Iraola

Ten outfield players were seen working directly with former United States boss Pochettino in the footage, though it seems unlikely they will all start Sunday's match.

"We've faced each other and obviously he [Pochettino] has a lot of Premier League games behind him that we can look at," said Iraola.

"We can look at games from the US but it's true that they have this small advantage that we don't have references to prepare, because they can go different ways that we honestly don't know right now."

Iraola said he expected United to be "well prepared" as Pochettino's assistants travelled to England to work with the players before the Argentine arrived on Wednesday.

"They have this advantage that we don't exactly know - or at least we don't have the references like we do against other opposition," he said.

"Especially the beginning of the game will be important. We have to adapt to certain things. But we know the players very well."

Liverpool are fourth in the table - 14 places ahead of United.

But they have failed to beat the Red Devils at Anfield in each of the past three seasons, and have lost to Arsenal and Manchester City at home already in this campaign.

"You don't find bigger games than this," said Iraola. "I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be a part of these games.

"We have to acknowledge the importance of the game. There are a lot of ingredients. They have a new manager, new challenges for us. This is important for us in a lot of different ways.

"We want to improve our form at home. We have been very good away but not good at home and the first chance we have is United on Sunday."

Arsenal currently sit top of the Premier League, five points clear of Brighton in second

Mikel Arteta says his Arsenal players have been warned against inadvertently leaking team news via Fantasy Premier League.

The intervention comes after Christos Tzolis selected and captained himself in his Fantasy Premier League (FPL) team before Arsenal's match against Liverpool on 1 November, after he had missed a month through injury.

The Gunners manager picked the winger in Arsenal's starting XI at Anfield in what was his first appearance since Greece's Nations League draw with the Netherlands on 1 October.

Before Saturday's match at Newcastle, Arteta said he had to speak to his squad, and those close to the club, about their FPL selections.

"With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well," he said

"They're constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It's a topic.

"This is the kind of thing that is happening in our society right now. It's something new. We haven't dealt with it before and we need to put new things in place.

"Obviously, confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. We'll take measures to make sure it doesn't happen."

The Spaniard also said his players are restricted from selecting themselves in their FPL line-ups.

#775. NASA reveals Earth's ozone hole has grown to a size not seen in a decade

Unusual weather patterns over Antarctica caused the ozone hole to expand dramatically in 2026, reaching one of its largest sizes on record. Despite the striking increase, scientists from NASA and NOAA say Earth's protective ozone layer is continuing its gradual recovery and remains on track to heal later this century.

The 2026 Antarctic ozone hole ranked as the seventh-largest in 48 years of observations, based on its average seasonal area. Scientists attributed the expansion primarily to an exceptionally strong polar vortex, a large circulation of winds that influences atmospheric conditions over Antarctica. They also emphasized that international efforts to reduce harmful chemicals have prevented the hole from becoming even larger.

Between September 7 and October 13, 2026, when ozone depletion was at its seasonal peak, the hole covered an average of approximately 9.6 million square miles (25 million square kilometers). That is more than twice the size of the United States. Scientists closely monitor ozone in the stratosphere because it serves as Earth's natural "sunscreen," protecting living organisms from dangerous solar radiation. Unlike this beneficial layer high in the atmosphere, ozone near Earth's surface is a pollutant frequently associated with human activities.

Antarctica's Ozone Hole Reaches Its Largest Size in a Decade

The ozone hole reached its maximum extent on September 18, spreading across 10.5 million square miles (27.1 million square kilometers). This was approximately 90% of the size of the largest ozone hole ever measured, which occurred on September 9, 2000.

"The annual ozone hole has been forming later in the season in recent years, which tells us the ozone layer is healing," said Paul Newman, a senior scientist at the University of Maryland and longtime leader of NASA's ozone research team at the agency's Goddard Space Flight Center. "But an unusually powerful polar vortex has extended ozone depletion in the Antarctic this season, allowing the hole to grow to proportions we haven't seen in a decade."

Although the hole expanded to an extraordinary size, the results also demonstrate the benefits of decades of international environmental protections. Without reductions in chemicals known to destroy ozone, the affected area could have been substantially greater.

"The 2026 ozone hole is large but could have been 1 to 2 million square miles (3.5 million square kilometers) larger if ozone-depleting substances were as prevalent in the atmosphere today as they were at their year 2000 peak," Newman said.

How a Powerful Polar Vortex Accelerates Ozone Loss

Ozone depletion begins with chemicals released through human activities, particularly compounds containing chlorine and bromine. Atmospheric circulation transports these substances into the stratosphere, where ultraviolet radiation breaks them apart. The released chlorine and bromine atoms then participate in chemical reactions involving particles in Antarctic stratospheric clouds, leading to the destruction of ozone.

A major factor in this process is the stratospheric polar vortex, a seasonal band of strong winds that circles Antarctica. This circulation traps extremely cold air over the region, allowing the formation of the special clouds that help trigger ozone destruction. When the vortex becomes unusually strong or expansive, conditions favorable for ozone loss can persist across a larger area.

In 2026, atmospheric disturbances that would normally weaken the vortex were unusually subdued. This allowed the circulation to remain powerful and helped create a broader region where ozone could be destroyed.

"The polar vortex was unusually large this year in part because planetary-scale weather systems that typically well up from the lower atmosphere and break up the vortex were especially weak in August and September," said Amy Butler, a research scientist at the NOAA Chemical Sciences Laboratory. "That weak wave action kept the strongest polar vortex winds further from the South Pole by several degrees of latitude, creating a larger area for conditions ideal for ozone depletion to occur."

NASA and NOAA Measure the 2026 Ozone Hole

Despite its exceptional geographic size, the 2026 ozone hole did not experience the same extreme levels of ozone loss observed during record-breaking events 10 or 20 years earlier.

To measure ozone concentrations, NOAA researchers launched instruments attached to weather balloons from the South Pole Baseline Atmospheric Observatory. They also collected readings using the Dobson Ozone Spectrophotometer, an optical device designed to measure atmospheric ozone. Their observations showed that ozone levels directly above the South Pole fell to their lowest reading of 2026 on October 17, reaching 105 Dobson units.

The Dobson unit is the standard measurement used to describe the total amount of ozone above a particular location. To illustrate the scale, 100 Dobson units would produce a layer of ozone just 1 millimeter thick, approximately the thickness of a dime, if all the ozone in the atmospheric column were compressed to standard temperature and pressure at sea level. The lowest ozone concentration ever measured over the South Pole was 92 Dobson units in October 2006.

Satellites provide another essential source of information. Since 1979, spaceborne instruments have helped scientists observe changes in the ozone layer and track its condition over time. The 2026 measurements included data from NASA's Aura satellite, NOAA-20, NOAA-21, and the Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership satellite, a joint NASA and NOAA mission.

Why Earth's Ozone Layer Is Still Recovering

Scientists say the latest observations reinforce evidence that international restrictions on ozone-destroying chemicals are working. Much of that progress can be traced to the Montreal Protocol, a global agreement adopted in 1987 to phase out substances responsible for damaging the ozone layer.

Under the agreement, countries committed to replacing harmful compounds such as chlorofluorocarbons with alternatives that pose less danger to atmospheric ozone. According to Stephen Montzka, a senior scientist at NOAA's Global Monitoring Laboratory, chlorine concentrations in the Antarctic stratosphere associated with ozone-depleting chemicals have declined by approximately one-third compared with their peak levels in the 1980s.

These reductions are significant because chlorofluorocarbons and other ozone-depleting compounds were once common in refrigerators, air conditioning systems, building insulation, and other everyday products. Although many of these substances have been phased out, they can remain in the atmosphere for decades. Additional emissions can also occur when older equipment, materials, and landfill waste release chemicals that were manufactured years ago.

Because these compounds break down so slowly, repairing the ozone layer takes many decades. Nevertheless, continued monitoring by NASA and NOAA indicates that the long-term recovery is progressing. Even with unusually large seasonal ozone holes such as the one observed in 2026, scientists expect the Antarctic ozone hole to recover by the 2070s.

The latest findings illustrate how exceptional atmospheric conditions can temporarily produce severe ozone depletion without reversing decades of environmental progress. They also highlight the lasting impact of international cooperation in protecting Earth's atmosphere.
